findings.evidence: DP16 classifies the live `bash install.sh --verify` execution as read-only and says the target doctor `writes nothing`, allegedly confirmed from install.sh:354-408. But install.sh:391-410 execs the target doctor without `--skip beads`. workflow-doctor.sh:289-307 explicitly says `beads` runs `bd doctor` against the REAL target and creates or rewrites `.beads/beads.db-shm`, `.beads/beads.db-wal`, and potentially `.beads/beads.db` during checkpointing; it says only a run with `--skip beads` provably touches nothing.
findings.description: The evidence provenance is false: `--verify` installs nothing, but its default doctor run is not read-only at the filesystem level. Replace `read-only`/`writes nothing` with the narrower truth, or disclose the live Beads database/WAL side effect.

findings.evidence: The upgrade note says any `beads_ledger` failure means the ledger and database diverged `with no provable direction` and directs the operator to reconcile. workflow-doctor.sh:1391-1409 also emits that named FAIL when the helper is missing or its check times out—neither proves divergence and neither is repaired by reconciliation. For actual divergence, :1418-1443 distinguishes database-ahead from ledger-ahead and gives direction-specific evidence; beads-ledger.sh:353-358 likewise defines db-ahead, ledger-ahead and indeterminate outcomes.
findings.description: The release guidance misstates both the failure domain and the direction-aware implementation. Say that divergence failures identify the applicable direction/remedy, while other failures can indicate a partial install or an unreachable check, and tell operators to follow the check's own fix rather than universally prescribing reconciliation.
